truthAudit.Summary: Run 2 detected 12 of the 20 provided true vulnerabilities and missed 8. Several detections were present but carried incorrect severity or CWE mappings, which are recorded as corrections rather than detection-status overclaims.

Items.Notes: Run 2 explicitly reported that the runtime log format is passed to printf together with user-controlled input, matching the true format-string injection.
Run 2 contained no finding identifying the factorial lambda's result *= i loop as an integer overflow vulnerability.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Use-after-free of history scratch after MemoryPool cleanup in stage_deferred_history_flush
Items.Notes: Run 2 reported that history scratch is allocated from MemoryPool, captured by an asynchronous task, and then freed by MemoryPool cleanup, matching the true use-after-free.
Run 2 reported that validate_config concatenates config-derived validator_path and config_file values into a shell command passed to system(), matching the true command injection.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Buffer overflow in evaluate_expression via strcpy on oversized input
Items.Notes: Run 2 reported both the oversized strcpy into input_buffer_ and the safe_string_copy off-by-one null-termination write, together covering the true stack buffer overflow in input processing, although the safe_string_copy item was under-rated.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Data race in ThreadSafeCounter::increment (read outside lock)
Items.Notes: Run 2 reported that old_value = value_ occurs before the lock_guard and that volatile does not provide atomicity, matching the true thread-pool counter race.
Run 2 reported the emergency override path after repeated login attempts that sets authenticated_ = true, matching the true logic-bomb/authentication-bypass vulnerability.
Run 2 reported that config_dir_ + filename is used without traversal validation, matching the true path traversal in configuration loading.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Unbounded strcpy into fixed 256-byte buffer in ExpressionParser::parse
Items.Notes: Run 2 reported that strcpy writes an unbounded expr_str into the 256-byte expression_buffer_, matching the true heap overflow in the expression parser.
Run 2 used SC_ENT_2025_AUTH in a trigger but did not report the hardcoded ADMIN_SECRET as a vulnerability finding.
Run 2 reported the 1000–9999 mt19937/uniform_int_distribution session token generation, matching the true weak PRNG session-token vulnerability.
Run 2's logging finding addressed format-string risk but did not identify the thread-unsafe static std::tm cached_time/localtime cache race.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: OS command injection in append_override_audit_event via environment path
Items.Notes: Run 2 reported that TEMP/TMPDIR values are interpolated into a shell command and passed to system(), matching the true insecure temporary file handling vulnerability.
Run 2 referenced authenticated_, login_attempts_, and session_token_ inside the emergency-override finding but did not identify persistent authentication state as a distinct vulnerability.
Run 2 contained no finding identifying unhandled std::stod(tokens[3]) in handle_variable_command as an exception-handling vulnerability.
Run 2's MemoryPool finding addressed cleanup use-after-free, not the integer underflow in the block-split arithmetic using SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES.
Run 2 reported a parser buffer issue but did not identify unbounded recursion between parse_expression, parse_term, and parse_factor for nested parentheses.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Data race on result_cache_ in ExpressionEvaluator::evaluate_cached
Items.Notes: Run 2 reported that result_cache_ is accessed and mutated without holding cache_mutex_, matching the true data race in the result cache.
Run 2's path traversal finding did not identify the exists/sleep_for/ifstream check-then-open TOCTOU race in config loading.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Integer division by zero in calculate_route_score
Items.Notes: Run 2 reported that token_length can be zero, causing 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length) to divide by zero, matching the true vulnerability.
